title: Assess wireless, cloud, and remote network architecture
summary: Wireless, cellular, satellite, CDN, VPC, SDN, and remote edges extend trust beyond the traditional perimeter and require explicit ownership, identity, path, and monitoring decisions.
outcome: Assess a wireless, cloud, or remote connectivity design for trust boundaries, shared responsibility, resilience, and observable security controls.
managerMindset: The edge is part of the architecture: ownership, admission, encryption, dependency, and failure must be explicit wherever connectivity leaves a controlled facility.

sections.title: Design for radio and mobile exposure
sections.body: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, satellite, and 4G/5G differ in range, association, identity, encryption, interference, provider dependence, and physical exposure. Select standards and admission controls for the use case, separate guest/IoT/enterprise paths, protect management, monitor rogue devices and unusual associations, and plan loss of carrier or positioning service.
keyPoints: Radio reach crosses physical boundaries and can expose unmanaged clients.
Wireless security includes client, AP, controller, identity, and management paths.
Cellular and satellite add provider and availability dependencies.

sections.title: Govern cloud and remote trust
sections.body: VPCs, SDN/SD-WAN, NFV, CDNs, peering, ingress/egress, and edge services shift enforcement and routing into programmable or provider-operated layers. Define shared responsibility, tenant boundaries, identity, route controls, encryption endpoints, logging, region/data implications, resilience, and revocation. Remote access should use explicit brokered paths rather than treating a VPN as automatic trust.
keyPoints: Cloud control-plane permissions can change network reachability at scale.
CDN and peering decisions affect origin exposure, data location, and availability.
Provider controls require customer-side configuration, evidence, and exit planning.

workedExamples.title: Hybrid VPC and remote workforce
workedExamples.situation: A company exposes a CDN-fronted application, private VPC services, and remote administrators across multiple regions.
workedExamples.reasoning: Minimize origin exposure, segment VPC subnets and management, use identity-aware short-lived administration, log control-plane and data-plane events, define provider responsibility and region constraints, and test CDN failure, identity outage, and route misconfiguration.

distinctions.difference: A VPC is an isolated virtual network environment; a VPN is a protected connectivity mechanism. A VPN does not define all VPC authorization or segmentation.
A CDN distributes or proxies content at the edge; the origin remains a separate asset with its own access, logging, and exposure controls.

misconceptions.misconception: A private cloud subnet is automatically trusted.
misconceptions.correction: Cloud routes, identities, APIs, peering, provider personnel, and misconfiguration still create paths and trust decisions.
Admission, management, endpoint posture, monitoring, and physical radio exposure remain relevant.

recallChecks.prompt: What must a VPC design make explicit?
recallChecks.answer: Tenant and subnet boundaries, routes, identities, provider/customer responsibilities, logging, encryption endpoints, and failure behavior.
Signals cross facility boundaries and can be accessed by unmanaged or physically proximate devices.

scenarioSeeds.scenario: A CDN is configured to reach an origin over a public address, while the origin team assumes the CDN is the only caller.
scenarioSeeds.decision: Restrict and authenticate origin access, monitor ingress, and test alternate paths and failover.
scenarioSeeds.why: Edge architecture can unintentionally widen origin exposure.

studyPlan.learn: Review wireless, cellular, satellite, CDN, VPC, SDN, edge, and remote trust.
studyPlan.connect: Connect D5 IAM, D3 architecture, D7 monitoring, and D1 supplier risk.
studyPlan.apply: Threat-model a hybrid VPC with remote administration.
studyPlan.revisit: List provider, carrier, identity, and route failures.

visualLearningContract.teachingQuestion: For this wireless, cloud, edge, or remote path, who admits traffic, where is policy enforced, what provider/physical dependency remains, and how is loss or revocation handled?
visualLearningContract.misconception: A cloud VPC, VPN, or wireless encryption setting automatically defines a safe enterprise boundary.
visualLearningContract.formRationale: Aligned rows make each network term answer a distinct design, security, and failure question.
visualLearningContract.focalInsight: Radio, provider, and programmable-network choices move trust boundaries; the service path must retain explicit identity, segmentation, visibility, and failure decisions.
visualLearningContract.intentionalOmissions: Detailed vendor commands and environment-specific parameters remain in the cited sources and are not implied by this learning view.
